newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-SPAIN'S GARRIDO MAKES SOLID START AT PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SPAIN'S GARRIDO MAKES SOLID START AT PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Spain's Ignacio Garrido, one of Europe's fast rising young players, celebrated his first round ever on American soil with a solid even-par 70 at Winged Foot in Thursday's opening round of the PGA Championship.

The 25-year-old Garrido, runner-up in his last two events on the European Tour and winner of the German Open earlier in the season, nearly finished the day under-par on the daunting layout before falling back with a two-putt bogey from four feet on the last hole.

"Level par or so is a great score on this course," said Garrido, who was invited to join the 150-man field just one week ago. "This might be the toughest course I have ever played. I have never played rough so severe as this."

Garrido, a near-lock to win a place on the European Ryder Cup team, bogeyed the third hole when he failed to get up and down from one of Winged Foots' deep greenside bunkers, but he rallied back with birdies at the fifth and seventh holes.
"This was my first round in the United States and my first visit to this country," said the slender Spaniard from Madrid.
"The conditions are great and I'm happy I performed quite well."
Garrido stands sixth on the European Ryder Cup table following his second place at the Scandinavian Masters and his joint second at last week's Czech Open.
Last year he ranked 47th on the tour's money list.
"This game is just unbelievable," said Garrido, whose father is a former Ryder Cup player. "You start playing well and you can do anything.
"When you're playing badly, you can't do anything."
